Rashi on Niddah 14a:10:1.hebrew: רצופה - מעוכה על העד, רחוק מן הדם קצת. ללישנא דבדוק, כיון דקים להו לרבנן דאין שם מאכולת, ודאי דם מגופה הוא, שהרי העד היה בדוק לה קודם הקינוח, ומאכולת (מעלמא הואי התם בעד שהיא רצופה). וללישנא דדחוק, איכא לספוקי שמא האי דם ממאכולת, ומתוך שדחוק הוא, מעכה השמש בשעת תשמיש:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:10:1.english: Squashed - Crushed on the examination cloth, slightly distant from the blood. According to the version of "examined": Since it is established to the Sages that there is no louse there, the blood is certainly from her body, for the cloth had been examined by her prior to the wiping, and the louse (came from elsewhere there onto the cloth, where it was squashed). And according to the version of "narrow": There is reason to doubt whether this blood is from a louse, and because [that place] is narrow, the [male] organ crushed it at the time of intercourse.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:11:1.english: And on the following day she found blood on her - On the thigh.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:12:1.hebrew: טמאה נדה - טומאה ודאית, דכיון דהעד בדוק לה שלא היה בו דם קודם בדיקה, ודאי מגופה אתאי על העד ומשם הוטח בירכה, ולא אמרינן דלמא מעלמא אתא על ירכה וספק טומאה היא:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:12:1.english: She is impure as a menstruating woman - [This means] definite impurity, for since the cloth was checked by her, [showing] that there was no blood on it prior to the examination, [the blood] certainly came from her body onto the cloth, and from there it was smeared onto her thigh; and we do not say: Perhaps it came from elsewhere onto her thigh, and it is an uncertain impurity.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:13:1.hebrew: ולמחר מצאה עליו דם - על העד, ואיכא לספוקי: דלמא מקמי הכי הוה ביה. להכי לא נקט הכא טחתו בירכה, דא"כ הוו להו תרי ספיקי לקולא: חדא, דלמא לאו מן העד הוטח על ירכה; ואפילו את"ל מן העד אתא, דלמא כיון דאינו בדוק מקמי הכי הוה:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:13:1.english: And on the following day she found blood on it - On the examination cloth, and there is reason to doubt: perhaps [the blood] was on it prior to this. For this reason, he did not state here, "she smeared it on her thigh," for if so, there would be two doubts toward leniency: one, perhaps [the blood] was not smeared onto her thigh from the cloth; and even if you say that it came from the cloth, perhaps, since it was not examined, [the blood] was [on it] prior to this.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:14:1.hebrew: משום נדה - טומאה ודאית, דכיון דחזקת דמים שם, לא מספקינן במקמי הכי:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:14:1.english: As a menstruating woman - Definite impurity, for since there is a presumption of blood there, we do not suspect [that it was on the cloth] prior to this.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:14:2.hebrew: משום כתם - כלומר טומאת ספק, ותולין:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:14:2.english: Due to a stain - That is to say, an uncertain impurity, and one suspends [the status of terumah].

Rashi on Niddah 14a:1:1.english: Camel riders - Their limbs become heated against the flesh of the camel, and they emit semen.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:1:2.english: All of them are wicked - As he said.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:1:3.hebrew: כולם צדיקים - שדרים בסכנה, ולבם לאביהם שבשמים:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:1:3.english: They are all righteous - For they live in danger, and their hearts are [turned] to their Father in Heaven.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:2:1.hebrew: דמכף - לשון אוכף של חמור. אם יש לו אוכף, האבר אינו מתחמם, שהעץ קשה הוא; ואם אין לו אוכף, מתחמם בבשר החמור. אבל דרך גמלים לרכוב בלא אוכף, אלא במרדעת, ומתחמם:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:2:1.english: That it is saddled - An expression for the saddle of a donkey. If it has a saddle, the organ does not become heated, because the wood is hard; and if it does not have a saddle, it becomes heated against the flesh of the donkey. However, it is the way with camels to ride without a saddle, but rather with a saddlecloth, and [the organ] becomes heated.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:2:2.hebrew: דמטרטין - ירך מכאן וירך מכאן, ואברו מתחמם:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:2:2.english: That they straddle - [With] a thigh on this side and a thigh on that side, and his organ becomes heated.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:2:3.english: That they do not straddle - He rides like a woman [sidesaddle].

Rashi on Niddah 14a:2:4.hebrew: מטרטין - לשון מאזנים, כדאמרי' במנחות (דף פז:): וכי טורטני יכניס:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:2:4.english: Weighing on scales - An expression of balance scales, as we say in Menachot (page 87b): "Would he bring in a balance scale?"

Rashi on Niddah 14a:3:1.hebrew: אפרקיד - פניו למעלה. וגנות הוא, שפעמים שיתקשה אבר תוך שינתו ויתגלה; ועוד, שידיו מונחות לו על אברו ומתחמם:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:3:1.english: Lying on his back - [With] his face turned upward. And it is disgraceful, as at times [his sexual] organ will become erect during his sleep and become exposed; and furthermore, his hands rest upon his organ and it becomes warmed.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:4:1.english: Leaning - Tilted slightly on his side.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:4:2.english: Even when he tilts, it is forbidden - Unless he is sitting or lying completely on his side.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:5:1.english: One for him and one for her - To wipe [themselves] after intercourse.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:5:2.hebrew: לתקן את הבית - כלומר, לבדוק לפני תשמיש ולהכין עצמה לבעלה. וה"ה לכל הנשים, כדתנן בפ"ק (לעיל נדה יא.): "ובשעה שהיא עוברת לשמש את ביתה". והא דנקט "צנועות" - כדמפרש בפ"ק: צנועות, עד שבודקת בו לפני תשמיש זה, אין בודקת בו לפני תשמיש אחר:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:5:2.english: To prepare the house - That is to say, to examine [herself] before intercourse and prepare herself for her husband. And the same applies to all women, as we learned in the mishna in the first chapter (above, Niddah 11a): "And at the time that she is about to engage in intercourse with her husband." And that which [the mishna] stated "modest women" is as [the Gemara] explains in the first chapter: Modest women—the examination cloth that she examines [herself] with before this intercourse, she does not examine [herself] with before another intercourse.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:6:1.hebrew: נמצא דם על שלו - ואפילו לאחר זמן, ששהה לאחר בעילה זמן ארוך קודם קינוח, בידוע שהיה דם בשעת תשמיש:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:6:1.english: [If] blood was found on his [cloth] - And even [if it was found] after [some] time, where he waited a long time after intercourse before wiping, it is known that there was blood at the time of intercourse.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:6:2.hebrew: טמאים - שניהם טומאת שבעה, כדין בועל נדה, כדכתיב (ויקרא ט״ו:כ״ד): ותהי נדתה עליו:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:6:2.english: [They are] impure - Both of them [contract] a seven-day impurity, in accordance with the law of one who has intercourse with a menstruating woman, as it is written (Leviticus 15:24): "And her menstrual impurity shall be upon him."

Rashi on Niddah 14a:6:4.hebrew: לאחר זמן - לאחר אותיום, טמאים מספק שניהם שבעה ימים. ומיהו טומאת ספק הוא — לתלות, אבל לא לשרוף:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:6:4.english: After [some] time - After otyom [immediately after intercourse], both of them are impure due to uncertainty for seven days. However, it is an impurity of uncertainty: to suspend [terumah], but not to burn [it].

Rashi on Niddah 14a:7:1.english: Her face - Her lower face [i.e., her pudenda].

Rashi on Niddah 14a:7:2.hebrew: ואח"כ - כלומר, שהתה יותר מכשיעור הזה, אחר אחר הוא זה:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:7:2.english: And afterward - That is to say, [if] she delayed more than this measure [of time], this is after the "after" [time].

Rashi on Niddah 14a:7:3.hebrew: מטמאות מעת לעת - טהרות ואדם במגע טומאת ערב, ומדרבנן, כדין מעת לעת, דאמר בפ"ק: ומה היא מטמאה? משכבה ומושבה. וכיון דעושה משכב ומושב לטמא אדם, כל שכן דהיא עצמה מטמאה אדם:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:7:3.english: They transmit impurity for a twenty-four-hour period - [They transmit impurity to] ritually pure items and a person through contact, with evening impurity, and [this is] by rabbinic law, in accordance with the law of a twenty-four-hour period, as [the Gemara] said in the first chapter: "And what does she render impure? Her bed and her seat. And since she renders a bed and a seat [impure] to render a person impure, all the more so she herself renders a person impure."

Rashi on Niddah 14a:7:4.english: And she does not transmit impurity to the one who had intercourse with her - [With] a seven-day impurity.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:7:5.hebrew: ר"ע אומר אף מטמאה את בועלה - ר"ע לטעמיה, דאמר כל מעת לעת מטמאה את בועלה מספק טומאת שבעה, בפ"ק (לעיל נדה ו.):
Rashi on Niddah 14a:7:5.english: Rabbi Akiva says: She even transmits impurity to the man who had intercourse with her - Rabbi Akiva follows his reasoning, as he said that [for] any twenty-four-hour period, she transmits impurity to the man who had intercourse with her, out of doubt, [with] a seven-day impurity, in the first chapter (above, Niddah 6a).

Rashi on Niddah 14a:9:1.hebrew: מאכולת - כינה. ואמאי טמאין ודאי, לשרוף תרומה ולהתחייב בקרבן ודאי? להוי ספק, לתלות תרומה ולהביא אשם תלוי ולא חטאת, דדלמא דם מאכולת הוא, שהיה באותו מקום באשה, וכשבעל נדבק בו:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:9:1.english: A louse - [Meaning] a louse. And why are they definitely impure, to burn *terumah* and to be liable for a definite sacrifice? Let it be a case of doubt, to suspend *terumah* and to bring a provisional guilt offering and not a sin offering, for perhaps it is the blood of a louse that was in that place in the woman, and when he engaged in intercourse, it stuck to him.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:9:2.hebrew: בדוק - דודאי אין שם מאכולת, ודם ודאי מגופה אתיא:
Rashi on Niddah 14a:9:2.english: Examined - For it is certain that there is no louse there, and the blood definitely came from her body.

Rashi on Niddah 14a:9:3.english: It is constricted - That a louse cannot enter there.

Tosafot on Niddah 14a:11:1.hebrew: וטחתו בירכה - פירוש, במקום שאין דם המקור יכול ליפול שם:
Tosafot on Niddah 14a:11:1.english: And she wiped it on her thigh - [The] explanation is: In a place where blood of the womb (makor) cannot fall [there].

Tosafot on Niddah 14a:11:2.hebrew: ולמחר מצאה עליה דם - ה"ג רש"י, פי' על ירכה. וקאמר דטמאה נדה, דאיכא למימר דמן העד נתלכלך ירכה, ולא מעלמא. וא"ת: ותבדוק העד? וי"ל: שנאבד העד. א"נ: שמא דם העד עצמו בא מדם ירכה, כיון שנמצא על העד רק במקום שנגע בירכה, וכגון שיש כגריס ועוד, דליכא חששא דמאכולת. [או שמא כיון שנמצא על ירכה במקום שנגע בעד מוכח מילתא שמחמת העד הוא וטמאה. גליון:] ודוקא בעד הבדוק לה; אבל בשאינו בדוק לה, הוי ספק ספקא, כדפי' רש"י. ודוקא טחתו בירכה; אבל הניחתו בקופסא, פשיטא דטמאה. ור"ח גרס: ומצאה עליו, פירוש: על העד; וטחתו בירכה היינו בגלוי, שלא הניחתו בקופסא, דבהניחתו בקופסא פשיטא דטמאה. ופריך: והא חוששין אמרת לן, דאימר מעלמא אתי:
Tosafot on Niddah 14a:11:2.english: And on the following day she found blood on her - This is the reading of Rashi, meaning on her thigh. And [Rav] says that she is impure as a menstruating woman (niddah), for one can say that her thigh was stained from the examination cloth, and not from an external source. And if you say: But let her examine the cloth? One can answer that the cloth was lost. Alternatively: Perhaps the blood on the cloth itself came from blood on her thigh, since it was found on the cloth only in the place where it touched her thigh; and [this is] for instance where there is [a stain] the size of a split-pea and more (ke-gris ve-od), so that there is no concern of a louse. [Or perhaps, since it was found on her thigh in the place that touched the cloth, the matter is proven that it is on account of the cloth, and she is impure. — Gloss] And [this is] specifically with a cloth that was examined by her; but with [a cloth] that was not examined by her, it is a double doubt (safek sefeika), as Rashi explained. And [this was stated] specifically where she pressed it against her thigh; but if she placed it in a box, it is obvious that she is impure. And Rabbeinu Chananel reads: "And she found upon it," meaning upon the cloth; and "she pressed it against her thigh" means [that it was left] exposed, in that she did not place it in a box, for had she placed it in a box, it would be obvious that she is impure. And [the Gemara] objects: "But didn't you tell us: one is [only] concerned?" — for say it came from an external source!

Tosafot on Niddah 14a:12:1.hebrew: אמר שמואל טמאה נדה - אפי' ר' חייא דמטהר בסמוך מודה הכא, דהא ר' חייא כר' יוסי ס"ל, ושמואל גופיה פסיק בהאשה (לקמן נדה נט:) כרבי יוסי, והכא קאמר דטמאה נדה:
Tosafot on Niddah 14a:12:1.english: Shmuel said: [She is] impure as a menstruating woman - Even Rabbi Ḥiyya, who deems [her] pure in the adjacent [case], concedes here; for Rabbi Ḥiyya holds in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, and Shmuel himself rules in [the chapter of] "HaIsha" (below, Niddah 59b) in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, and [yet] here [Shmuel] says that she is impure as a menstruating woman.

Tosafot on Niddah 14a:13:1.hebrew: בעד שאינו בדוק לה - נראה לפרש דידעה שהיה נקי לפני יום או יומים, ועתה בשעת בדיקה נטלתו ממקום המוצנע ולא בדקה העד; אבל אין נראה לפרש שלא היה בדוק מעולם, דבהא לא היה רבי מחזיק טומאה ודאי:
Tosafot on Niddah 14a:13:1.english: With a cloth that was not examined by her - It seems [correct] to explain that she knew that it was clean a day or two earlier, and now, at the time of the examination, she took it from a concealed place and did not examine the cloth; but it does not seem [correct] to explain that it had never been examined, for in that [case], Rebbi would not have maintained definite impurity.

Tosafot on Niddah 14a:1:1.hebrew: רוכבי גמלים אסורין לאכול בתרומה - ואע"ג דאמר שמואל בפ' יוצא דופן (לקמן נדה דף מג.): כל שכבת זרע שאין כל גופו מרגיש אינו מטמא — הכא, דלמא הרגיש כל גופו ולאו אדעתיה:
Tosafot on Niddah 14a:1:1.english: Camel riders are forbidden to eat terumah - And even though Shmuel said in the chapter [entitled] "Yotzei Dofen" (below, Niddah 43a): "Any seminal emission regarding which one's entire body does not sense [it] does not transmit impurity" — here, perhaps his entire body did sense [it], but it was not to his awareness.

Tosafot on Niddah 14a:1:2.hebrew: רוכבי גמלים כולם רשעים החמרים מהן רשעים מהן צדיקים - וא"ת, דאמרינן בפרק עשרה יוחסין (קדושין דף פב.): גמלים רובן כשרים, חמרים רובן ליסטין? וי"ל, דהכא מיירי ברוכבים, ומשום הרהור; והתם לא מיירי ברוכבים, אלא בנותנין סחורה על הגמלים, והם הולכים ברגל רחוק, במקום סכנה; וחמרין [שהם ליסטים, משום דבשעה שקונים] עושין רמאות במשא ובמתן:
Tosafot on Niddah 14a:1:2.english: Camel riders are all wicked; donkey drivers, some of them are wicked, some of them are righteous - And if you say that we say in the chapter [entitled] 'Asarah Yuchasin' (Kiddushin 82a): Most camel drivers are upright, [and] most donkey drivers are bandits? One can answer that here it is dealing with riders, and [this is] because of [improper] thoughts (hirhur); whereas there, it is not dealing with riders, but rather with those who place merchandise upon the camels and they walk on foot far away, in a place of danger; and [as for] donkey drivers [who are called 'bandits,' it is because when they buy,] they practice deceit in business.

Tosafot on Niddah 14a:3:1.hebrew: אפרקיד - פי' הקונטרס: פניו למעלה. וכן משמע בהמוכר את הספינה (ב"ב דף עד.), גבי מתי מדבר דגנו אפרקיד, וחליף טייעא תותי ברכייהו ורומחא בידיה. ולשון אפרקיד: אפורייאה קדל (קדקדא). ולא כפירוש הערוך, דפי' פניו מטה, ולשון אפרקיד: אפוי קיד; ועוד קשה: רי"ש דאפרקיד למה לי? [וע"ע תוספות פסחים קח. ד"ה פרקדן]:
Tosafot on Niddah 14a:3:1.english: [Lying] on his back [aperkeid] - Rashi explained: [With] his face upward. And so it is implied in [the chapter] HaMokher Et HaSefinah (Bava Batra 74a) regarding the Dead of the Wilderness, who were sleeping aperkeid, and an Arab [merchant] passed beneath their knees with a spear in his hand. And the term aperkeid [is a contraction of]: a-furyah kedal [on the bed lies the nape of the neck] (or kodkeda [the crown of the head]). And not like the explanation of the Arukh, who explained [that it means with] his face downward, and the term aperkeid [is a contraction of]: appoi keid [his face is bowed down]; and furthermore, it is difficult: why do I need the [letter] resh of aperkeid? [And see further Tosafot, Pesachim 108a, s.v. Perakdan.]

Tosafot on Niddah 14a:3:2.hebrew: לייט אמאן דגני אפרקיד - פי' בקונטרס, שידיו מונחות על מילתו ומתחמם. ורשב"ם פירש, שבגדיו נופלין על אמתו ומתחמם. ומה שפי' עוד, שפעמים [מתקשה ומתגלה], לא נראה; דבבית סגור או אפל, מאי א"ל? [ועוד שמעתי, כששוכב אפרקיד מתחמם השדרה, ומחמת זה יתקשה האבר ויבא לידי קרי. גליון:]
Tosafot on Niddah 14a:3:2.english: He curses one who sleeps lying on his back - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained that his hands rest upon his circumcision [i.e., his organ] and it becomes heated. And Rashbam explained that his garments fall upon his organ and it becomes heated. And that which he [Rashi] further explained, that at times [the organ] becomes erect and uncovered, does not seem [correct], for in a closed or dark room, what is there to say? [And furthermore I heard: When one lies on his back, the spine becomes heated, and on account of this the organ becomes erect and he will come to a seminal emission. — Gloss.]

Tosafot on Niddah 14a:4:1.hebrew: ק"ש כי מצלי אסור - היינו כשהוא קצת אפרקיד, אבל על צדו לגמרי שרי; כדאמר בפ' מי שמתו (ברכות דף כד.): שנים שהן ישנים במטה, זה הופך פניו לכאן וזה הופך פניו לכאן, וקורין ק"ש:
Tosafot on Niddah 14a:4:1.english: [Reciting] Shema when one tilts is forbidden - That is, when he is slightly on his back (afarkid); but [lying] completely on his side is permitted, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter "Mi She-Meto" (Berakhot 24a): "Two [people] who are sleeping in a bed, this one turns his face here and that one turns his face here, and they recite Shema."

Tosafot on Niddah 14a:9:1.hebrew: וליחוש דלמא דם מאכולת הוא - אבל על בדיקות דמטמאינן לה אם מצא דם, לא פריך, דדלמא חומרא היא; אבל הכא פריך: אמאי חייבין בקרבן? דלמא מייתי חולין בעזרה. ועוד נראה, וכן פר"ח, דפריך אנמצא על שלו, כי לא נמצא על שלה: אמאי מטמאין, כיון דאיכא הוכחה דלא אתי מגופה:
Tosafot on Niddah 14a:9:1.english: And let us be concerned that perhaps it is the blood of a louse - However, regarding examinations where we declare her impure if blood was found, [the Gemara] does not object, for perhaps [this] is [merely] a stringency. But here it objects: Why are they liable to [bring] an offering? Perhaps he is bringing non-sacred [animals] into the Temple Courtyard (chullin ba'azarah)! And furthermore it seems [plausible], and so explained Rabbeinu Chananel, that it objects regarding [the case where blood was] found on his [cloth] when it was not found on hers: Why do they declare [them] impure, since there is proof that it did not come from her body?

Tosafot on Niddah 14a:9:2.hebrew: דחוק הוא אצל מאכולת - אין לפרש שאינה יכולה ליכנס אלא בדוחק, ולפעמים נכנסת; דא"כ, הוה ליה למימר בסמוך ללישנא דדחוק הוא: אימר איתרמויי איתרמי, ולמה צריך להזכיר דשמש רצפה? לכך י"ל: בדוק הוא — שאינה באה כלל סמוך לרחם מפני הזוהמא, שיוכל השמש להכניס; ודחוק הוא אצל מאכולת — היינו דאינה נכנסת בשום פנים מאליה, אלא שפעמים שמתקרבת לרחם כ"כ, עד שהשמש מכניסה ומרצפה:
Tosafot on Niddah 14a:9:2.english: [That place] is constricted regarding a louse - One should not explain that it cannot enter except with difficulty, and [yet] sometimes enters; for if so, shortly [in the Gemara], regarding the version of "it is constricted," it should have said: "Say that it happened to occur [that it entered]," and why did it need to mention that the organ crushed it? Therefore, it can be said: "It is examined" — that it does not come near the womb at all on account of the foul discharge, such that the organ could bring [it] in; and "it is constricted regarding a louse" — that means that it does not enter on its own under any circumstances, but rather that sometimes it approaches the womb so closely that the organ brings it inside and crushes it.
